topic: A person learns their apartment building is going condo
text: Words don't form right. They clump, heavy, in my throat. Can't they see the walls closing in? This place, my place—now fenced with finer, harder lines. Promises of polish, of privacy, but it's a trap. They whisper of choice, of ownership, but it's a sly shift, a slow steal. Every door a reminder, every step through the halls a tread on borrowed ground. What was once shared, now sliced and sold. They speak of change and new beginnings, but it feels like a chase, a relentless push from the only path I knew. I move through these halls, a shadow in my own home, eyes narrow, jaw set tight.
